visual_observations.method: Met image search on 2026-11-09 displayed official original DP105850.jpg thumbnail in response; Matched original filename and work accession with Met official record. Thumbnail is a crop/preview and not complete inspection of all reverse-side panels.
visual_observations.observed: Gold-ground screen composition with large pine branches and trunk, groups of child-like figures drawing a wheeled flower cart amid pale pink/white blossoms, pale gold clouds and decorative painting. Number/identity of gods taken from Met's scholarly Overview rather than guessed from thumbnail.

separate_pass_review.method: After drafting, reread Met45217 Overview and Artwork Details separately, checking the specific three named deities, Chinese children's auspicious themes, peonies, dates, 6-panel format, and matching primary image preview. Avoided attributing depicted happiness to author's feelings or suggesting seven deities are all visible.
separate_pass_review.limitations: Same assistant independent pass, not external reviewer. Web image shows Met primary DP105850 thumbnail only; reversed panels and full-resolution source not inspected in this session. Registered full byte hashes from October 2026 retained.

checks.finding: Met45217/29.100.498: Kano Chikanobu; 17th–18th century six-panel screen, ink/color/gilt on paper.
Met describes precisely Daikoku, Ebisu, Hotei and the Chinese-child auspicious motif; no false assertion that all seven gods appear.
Emotion tags remain 0: auspicious subject is not proof the artist felt personal joy.
New Japanese visitor text constructed from object-specific interpretation and visual observation; not copied or paragraph-by-paragraph translated from Met commentary.
